thread.title: Chipmakers Silicon Labs, STMicro Deliver Upbeat Quarterly Reports

author: PATRICK SEITZ
title: Chipmakers Silicon Labs, STMicro Deliver Upbeat Quarterly Reports
text:
Diversified chipmakers Silicon Laboratories ( SLAB ) and STMicroelectronics ( STM ) on Wednesday reported solid March-quarter results and gave upbeat guidance, providing good news for the embattled semiconductor sector.
X
Silicon Labs stock jumped 7% to close at 95.20 on the stock market today . STMicro gained 3.2% to 21.99.
Austin, Texas-based Silicon Labs earned an adjusted 87 cents a share, up 38% year over year, on sales of $205 million, up 15%, in the first quarter . Analysts expected earnings of 76 cents a share on sales of $199 million.
For the current quarter, the company forecasts earnings of an adjusted 84 cents a share, up 6%, on sales of $214 million, up 13%, based on the midpoint of its guidance. Wall Street had predicted earnings of 83 cents a share on sales of $206 million.

Silicon Labs makes chips for automotive, industrial and consumer applications. Its products include microcontrollers, sensors and wireless communications chips.
French-Italian chipmaker STMicroelectronics earned 26 cents a share, up 117% year over year, on sales of $2.23 billion, up 22%, in the first quarter. Earnings and revenue were in line with views.
"We delivered a better than seasonal performance in Automotive and Industrial, thanks to our application-focused approach on Smart Driving and Internet of Things, despite the anticipated unfavorable seasonal dynamics for smartphone applications," STMicro Chief Executive Carlo Bozotti said in a news release .
For the second quarter, STMicro is targeting sales of about $2.26 billion, up 17% year over year. Wall Street was predicting $2.25 billion.
It expects a gross profit margin of 40%, compared with 37.6% in the year-earlier quarter.
"Despite the weak demand we are experiencing for smartphones in the first half of 2018, we anticipate second quarter and first half revenues to grow year-over-year about 17.5% and 19.8%, respectively, at the midpoint of our guidance range," Bozotti said. "This will be driven by the continued better than seasonal sales trends in Automotive, Industrial and Internet of Things applications."
He said he sees "healthy demand" across all product groups and end markets, including smartphones, in the second half of the year.
Chipmakers Battered On Tuesday, the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index lost 0.8%, its fifth straight loss, to close below its 200-day moving average for the first time since June 2016. The index was up 0.2% midday on Wednesday.
Chip stocks have been battered in recent trading sessions following disappointing quarterly reports last week from Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing ( TSM ), Lam Research ( LRCX ) and ASML Holding ( ASML ).
Chipmakers with exposure to the smartphone market, especially Apple 's ( AAPL ) iPhone, have been particularly hard hit because of weakening handset sales.
Late Tuesday, chipmaker Texas Instruments ( TXN ) and chip-gear supplier MKS Instruments ( MKSI ) cheered investors with better-than-expected results for the first quarter .
Cree Jumps On Earnings Beat Chipmaker Cree ( CREE ) late Tuesday beat expectations for its fiscal third quarter ended March 25.
Durham, N.C.-based Cree earned an adjusted 4 cents a share, vs. 1 cent in the year-earlier period, on sales of $356 million, up 4%, in the March quarter. Analysts expected Cree to earn an adjust 1 cent a share on sales of $354 million in the period.
Cree shares slipped 0.3% to close at 39.25 on Wednesday.
Cree makes power-switching and radio-frequency chips as well as light-emitting diodes.
The company gave mixed guidance for the current quarter. It expects to earn an adjusted 7 cents a share, up 75% year over year, on sales of $400 million, up 11%, based on the midpoint of guidance, in the June quarter. Analysts were modeling 8 cents and $383 million.
